title: HD20-2000 Series IoT Controller | Digital & Analogue I/O | Hitelecom
metaDescription: HD20-2000 series IoT controller with a 2DO + 2DI + 2AI configuration, edge processing, local and remote control, dual watchdogs and Hitelecom Cloud monitoring.
heroValue:
Connect field signals.
Control with context.
heroDescription: The Hitelecom HD20-2000 series brings field data acquisition, equipment monitoring and local, remote or condition-based control into a compact RTU. A 2DO + 2DI + 2AI configuration connects equipment states, external measurement signals and control circuits. Edge processing, remote configuration and firmware upgrades support deployment and maintenance, with monitoring data available through Hitelecom Cloud. The 4G model illustrated is HD20-4021GD.
reviewNotice: Configuration reference: 2 digital outputs, 2 digital inputs and 2 analogue inputs. Select signal types, electrical limits, communication settings and installation requirements for the ordered configuration.

interfaceCards.title: Digital outputs
interfaceCards.text: Send control signals to compatible equipment control circuits. Match the output type, load interface and local operating priority to the installation.

interfaceCards.title: Digital inputs
interfaceCards.text: Read equipment states through compatible digital signals. Give each input a defined normal state and an operational meaning.

interfaceCards.title: Analogue inputs
interfaceCards.text: Acquire measurement signals from compatible external transmitters. Select the input range and scaling for the instrument and working range.

features.title: Digital and analogue I/O together
features.text: A 2DO + 2DI + 2AI configuration combines equipment-state acquisition, external measurement inputs and output commands in one controller. Match the channel allocation to the equipment signal list.

features.title: Edge processing at the equipment
features.text: Process field information close to its source for equipment monitoring and condition-based actions. The project configuration defines the signal interpretation, control conditions and permitted responses.

features.title: Local, remote and condition-based control
features.text: Use the operating mode that fits the task: local operation, remote supervision or an action linked to a configured condition. Define priorities and equipment feedback for the selected control arrangement.

features.title: Master/slave operating modes
features.text: Support project-defined device coordination with master/slave working modes. The selected interface, communication protocol and device roles form part of the integration configuration.

features.title: Online monitoring and threshold alerts
features.text: Use Hitelecom Cloud to view uploaded monitoring data online and receive alerts when configured thresholds are exceeded. Map equipment states, measurement units and alert recipients to the operating workflow.

features.title: Remote configuration and upgrades
features.text: Adjust supported settings and upgrade device firmware remotely. Plan maintenance around the installed configuration, software version and the site’s operating procedure.

features.title: Hardware and software watchdogs
features.text: Dual watchdog mechanisms support recovery from defined software or system faults. Recovery behaviour and output states are part of the device configuration and commissioning checks.

features.title: Compact integration for field equipment
features.text: Bring monitoring and control into equipment rooms, service cabinets and distributed installations with a compact controller design. Select the power, enclosure and wiring arrangement for the site.

workflow.title: Acquire the field signals
workflow.text: Bring digital equipment states and analogue transmitter signals into a common device configuration. Assign each point its source, units, range and normal state.

workflow.title: Apply the operating logic
workflow.text: Use local, remote or condition-based control for the application. Keep the device role, operating conditions and local equipment priorities explicit.

workflow.title: Issue the permitted action
workflow.text: Connect digital outputs to electrically compatible control circuits. Define the allowed equipment command and preserve the equipment’s independent protections.

workflow.title: Observe and verify the result
workflow.text: Read available equipment feedback and view uploaded monitoring data in Hitelecom Cloud. Test threshold alerts and distinguish an output command from the actual equipment outcome.

applicationsIntro: Connect equipment states, measurement signals and control circuits across eight application areas. Each task below is a selection example: allocate it against the 2DI / 2AI / 2DO reference I/O budget. Larger signal lists may require another configuration or additional controllers. External instruments and load-switching equipment are selected separately.

groups.title: Water & Pump Facilities
groups.intro: Bring pump states, level or pressure signals and permitted equipment commands into one site workflow. Keep motor protection and overflow protection in the appropriate local equipment system.
groups.imageAlt: Pumps, blue pipework and valves at a water facility

tasks.title: Pump run and fault monitoring
tasks.text: Read a pump’s run and fault indications so operators can distinguish the reported equipment states before arranging inspection.
tasks.interface: Allocate the two DI channels to compatible running and fault signals.
tasks.control: Use a DO for a permitted starter request where the external control circuit allows it.
tasks.verification: Check the actual run/fault contacts and local/remote priority; output activation alone is not running feedback.

tasks.title: Tank and sump level supervision
tasks.text: Combine an external level-transmitter signal with a discrete level event for tanks, sumps or service-water storage.
tasks.interface: Use a compatible AI signal for level and a DI for the selected level switch.
tasks.control: Apply a permitted pump or valve request within the approved level-control arrangement.
tasks.verification: Verify engineering units, switch orientation and physical feedback; independent high-level protection remains separate.

tasks.title: Valve command and position feedback
tasks.text: Keep a requested valve movement separate from its open or closed end-position feedback.
tasks.interface: Allocate DI points to available valve end-position contacts.
tasks.control: Connect DO points to a compatible actuator control interface and permitted operating sequence.
tasks.verification: Test full travel, local override and end-position feedback using the actuator’s operating requirements.

tasks.title: Pressure and leakage visibility
tasks.text: View an external pressure measurement alongside a selected leakage contact to give pump-room events a clear operating context.
tasks.interface: Use a compatible AI pressure signal and a DI leakage indication.
tasks.control: Configure threshold alerts and any permitted auxiliary indication separately from pump protection.
tasks.verification: Compare the displayed pressure with the source instrument and verify the leakage event at its physical location.

tasks.title: Two-pump operating-state comparison
tasks.text: Read the running indication from two pumps to help operators review which unit is operating and whether a planned changeover occurred.
tasks.interface: Allocate one DI to the run indication of each pump.
tasks.control: Keep duty selection and permitted start requests within the approved pump-control design.
tasks.verification: Compare reported states with the actual starters; additional fault points require additional suitable I/O.

groups.title: Buildings & HVAC
groups.intro: Connect selected building-services states and analogue measurements to facility monitoring and permitted supervisory actions. Match each task to the host equipment’s existing control interface.

tasks.title: Air-handling unit run and fault states
tasks.text: Give facility teams a consistent view of an air-handling unit’s reported running and fault conditions.
tasks.interface: Allocate DI points to compatible unit status signals.
tasks.control: Use a permitted enable request through the unit’s own control circuit.
tasks.verification: Verify actual operating feedback and local override; retain the unit’s sequencing and protections.

tasks.title: Filter and differential-pressure monitoring
tasks.text: Use a filter pressure switch or compatible pressure-transmitter output to support maintenance decisions for ventilation equipment.
tasks.interface: Select a DI switch signal or a compatible AI measurement for the chosen instrument.
tasks.control: Use configured alerts or an approved auxiliary indication for the maintenance event.
tasks.verification: Validate the switch setting or measurement scaling; a pressure event is not by itself an airflow measurement.

tasks.title: Plant-room door and leakage events
tasks.text: Identify selected access and leakage events under the correct plant-room or service-cabinet asset.
tasks.interface: Use the two DI channels for compatible door and leakage contacts.
tasks.control: Assign a DO to a suitable local indication circuit where required.
tasks.verification: Check normal-state logic, contact placement and event-to-location mapping.

tasks.title: Equipment enable and local priority
tasks.text: Add a permitted remote enable request while retaining the host equipment’s local operating priority.
tasks.interface: Use the documented enable interface and available mode or running feedback.
tasks.control: Select local, remote or condition-based action within the equipment’s allowed control scope.
tasks.verification: Test local override, command cancellation and the agreed response after restart.

tasks.title: Hydronic plant measurement points
tasks.text: Bring two compatible transmitter signals, such as circuit pressure and water temperature, into the building-services monitoring view.
tasks.interface: Allocate the two AI channels to selected externally conditioned measurement signals.
tasks.control: Use threshold alerts and permitted supervisory actions against the defined plant conditions.
tasks.verification: Verify both signals against the source instruments and keep their units and working ranges distinct.

groups.title: Industrial Equipment
groups.intro: Organize equipment signals around operating state, external measurements and the result of an authorized command. Machine control and safety functions remain with the appropriate equipment systems.

tasks.title: Machine running and fault indications
tasks.text: Make a machine’s selected auxiliary states available for production support and maintenance assessment.
tasks.interface: Allocate DI channels to approved machine running and fault signals.
tasks.control: Limit any DO connection to a machine function expressly intended for external supervision.

tasks.title: Compressor package supervision

tasks.interface: Use compatible package status contacts and their documented state meanings.
tasks.control: Provide a supervisory enable request only through the package’s approved control interface.
tasks.verification: Check actual running feedback, local mode and the package trip-reset policy.

tasks.title: Skid and auxiliary package alarms

tasks.control: Use an output only for an allowed package or auxiliary command.

faqs.q: What is the HD20-2000 series designed to do?
faqs.a: It combines field data acquisition, equipment monitoring and control in an IoT RTU. Digital inputs capture equipment states, analogue inputs receive compatible transmitter signals, and digital outputs connect to permitted control circuits. Edge processing, cloud monitoring and remote maintenance support the operating workflow.

The supplied series information lists a 2DO + 2DI + 2AI configuration: two digital outputs, two digital inputs and two analogue inputs. The series supports different I/O arrangements. Select the required channel allocation and obtain the electrical specification for the ordered configuration; the digits in an illustrated model name are not a substitute for that specification.

faqs.q: Which signals can the digital and analogue inputs accept?
faqs.a: DI points are used for compatible digital equipment states; AI points acquire compatible analogue transmitter signals. Electrical logic, input ranges, isolation and accuracy conditions must match the selected controller configuration and external instrument. Supply the instrument output specification when requesting a configuration.

The series supports local, remote and condition-based control. The application defines the permitted actions, operating conditions, equipment priorities and available feedback. Output electrical compatibility and independent equipment protections remain part of the installation design.

faqs.q: What do master/slave operating modes mean for integration?
faqs.a: They provide working roles for project-defined device coordination. Specify which device initiates the exchange, which responds and what data or commands are exchanged. The actual interface, communication protocol and supported operations are selected for the project; the role description alone does not define a particular protocol.

faqs.q: Can I view monitoring data and receive alerts in Hitelecom Cloud?
faqs.a: Yes. Hitelecom Cloud supports online viewing of uploaded monitoring data and alerts when configured thresholds are exceeded. Configure the measurement units, equipment-state meanings, limits and notification workflow for the connected points. Data availability and notification timing depend on the device reporting profile and network connection.

faqs.q: Can the controller be integrated with a customer platform?
faqs.a: Customer-platform integration is scoped around the device interface supported by the selected configuration. Agree the protocol, payload or point definitions, permitted commands and equipment-feedback mapping with the receiving platform. Hitelecom can assess these requirements during the project review.

faqs.q: What is the purpose of the two watchdog mechanisms?
faqs.a: The series uses hardware and software watchdog mechanisms to support recovery from defined faults. They are device-recovery features, not a guarantee of uninterrupted operation or a replacement for equipment protection. Commissioning should verify the applicable reset behaviour and the resulting output states.

faqs.q: Can settings and firmware be maintained remotely?
faqs.a: The series supports remote configuration and remote firmware upgrades. Use the settings and firmware intended for the delivered hardware configuration, and plan maintenance around the site operating procedure. Verify the required settings and device operation after the change.

faqs.q: What happens when communication or power is interrupted?
faqs.a: Local and condition-based control are supported operating modes, but lost-link operation, output fallback states and start-up recovery must be specified for the delivered configuration. A remote command path and an online monitoring view depend on connectivity. Test the agreed interruption and recovery behaviour at commissioning.

faqs.q: Can a digital output directly power a pump, fan or valve?
faqs.a: Select the connection using the output electrical type, the permitted load and the equipment interface. A suitable starter, contactor, intermediate switching device or actuator control circuit may be required. Output activation alone does not prove that a motor is running or a valve has reached position; use available equipment feedback.

faqs.q: What information is needed to select an installation configuration?
faqs.a: Provide the installation country, signal list, instrument output specifications, equipment-control interfaces, required local/remote priorities, power source and site conditions. Include the target platform and the expected behaviour during communication loss or restart. These details establish the I/O allocation, integration scope and any customization requirements.

enquiryIntro: Share the equipment signal list, instrument outputs, required control actions and installation conditions. We will help select the I/O arrangement, define the local and remote operating scope, and plan Hitelecom Cloud or customer-platform integration.
